title: docs(cursor): add lexical skill for document template filters
creator: yablonka-dev
summaryParagraphs: This PR adds a Lexical skill for document template filters. The new skill and references cover adding filters, Lexical React plugins, the matching engine, and the paste pipeline, making the document-template editing stack more discoverable for agents.

It also updates libraries/frontend/lexical-react/AGENTS.md, so local package guidance points agents toward the new skill. The change is documentation-heavy, mostly markdown, with no executable application code changes.

findings.text:
I'm having thoughts about whether you should be so specific about when to use it, down to the fine name granularity, versus providing a more high-level instruction. One of the sub-concerns here is that some new lexical file name will appear which is not mentioned in this description, and it will make the LLM bypass the skill because it doesn't match that file name

In other words, I believe you should mention which type of functionality and code _areas_ are covered by this skill, and less file names

findings.title: This is a strict workflow which often limits the harness's flexibility to find the right path bas...
findings.text:
This is a strict workflow which often limits the harness's flexibility to find the right path based on different scenarios. If time proved that this workflow is always similar, then all good. But, if you can think about corner cases that might call for deviating from this and improvising a better path based on different scenarios, then consider leaving here more flexibility.

This can be done by putting some guardrails, like:
- testing at the end
- testing at the start
- Definition of done checklist
- Ssome additional check point in the middle

And let it find the best path instead of following a rigid flow.

findings.title: We have very strict instructions here, down to the minute technical detail. Apart from limiting t...
findings.text:
We have very strict instructions here, down to the minute technical detail. Apart from limiting the harness's flexibility to make decisions, there is also the risk of 'drifting maintenance': We have now two versions of the code, If the real code changes, someone must take care to update the skill

Alternatively, I would consider leaving here pointers, clues, high-level instructions, and let the harness grep its way to the right files.
